voestalpine AG Names New Chief Financial Officer Amid Strategic Growth Plans

Austrian steelmaker voestalpine AG announced on Monday the appointment of Dr. Martin Weiss as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective September 1st. Weiss, who brings over two decades of experience in industrial finance, will join the Management Board, succeeding long-serving CFO Anna Berger, who is retiring after 12 years in the role.

The Linz-based company, a major employer in Upper Austria and supplier to automotive, railway, and construction sectors, described the appointment as part of its ongoing strategy to strengthen financial management and support global expansion. CEO Franz Koller stated, “Dr. Weiss’s proven track record in financial leadership and operational excellence will be instrumental as voestalpine continues its transformation to meet evolving market demands and sustainability goals.”

Analysts welcomed the news, highlighting Weiss’s background in capital market communications and M&A activity at the Austrian engineering group Eisenwerk Steyr. “Weiss’s experience is well suited to voestalpine’s ambitions, particularly as the company invests in decarbonization technologies and explores new market opportunities,” said Petra Leitner, steel industry analyst at Vienna-based consultancy Marktplatz Advisors.

The appointment comes as voestalpine AG reported stable revenues of €14.9 billion for its 2023/24 fiscal year, with operating profits of €1.35 billion, despite volatile raw material prices and global supply chain uncertainties. The company is currently undertaking a €1.2 billion investment in hydrogen-based steelmaking at its Linz facility, a project slated for completion in 2027.

The Austrian Steel Association commented, “Leadership continuity and financial expertise are critical for our member companies as they adapt to regulatory and technological shifts. We look forward to Dr. Weiss’s contributions at voestalpine.”

Weiss said in a statement, “I am honored to join voestalpine at this dynamic moment. My focus will be on maintaining financial resilience while supporting innovation and growth across our business units.”

Shares in voestalpine AG were up 0.8% at midday trading on the Vienna Stock Exchange following the announcement.
